papers.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
papers.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. papers.title: Making Tail Constraints Bind: Two Silent Failure Modes in CVaR-Constrained Portfolio RL
papers.summary: A portfolio allocator trained by reinforcement learning (RL) to maximise return has no reason to avoid large losses. papers.summary: Does reinforcement learning teach language models new capabilities, or merely amplify ones acquired during pre-training? papers.summary: Omnidirectional images (ODIs) are capable of showing the entire 360° of real-world scenes used in immersive fields of surveillance, robotics, and virtual reality. Most ODIs are obtained at low resolutions, which cause blurred edges, geometric distortions. papers.summary: Public outdoor mixed reality (MR) exhibitions make guidance a spatial interaction problem: visitors need timely explanations while roaming open sites, attending to virtual artworks, hazards, bystanders, and route choices. We present Dream-Butterfly, a field-deployed embodied conversational guide for campus-scale outdoor MR exhibitions. papers.title: Comb Machine: Mediated Intimacy in Telerobotics
papers.summary: Comb Machine: Almost Intimate (2025) is a teleoperated robotic installation in which a human comber remotely combs participants’ hair through a robot arm. Through delayed disclosure, participants first encounter the robot as seemingly autonomous and later discover the human labor behind the gesture. This mechanism changes the perceived agency and meaning of the experienced touch while heightening attention to hidden human labor behind automation. papers.title: ‘Photoshopping’ Robotic Movement for Human-Machine Creativity
papers.summary: This paper explores manipulating images through robotic motion rather than pixels. We used a motion capture system to record the trajectory of a calligraphy brush as an artist painted the classical Chinese orchid subject matter. We used this recording to recreate the painting with a robotic arm fitted with the same brush, then parametrically transformed the data to create new variations and experiments. This paper explores the creative agency of the artist, the motion editor, the robot and the physical materials, and how we might think of robotics as a domain for digital image editing.

Based on this process, we developed an AI-assisted interactive system using Along the River During the Qingming Festival. papers.title: FlexMARL: Graph-Driven Rollout-Training Co-Design for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Despite algorithm-level innovations for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the underlying infrastructure for large-scale MARL remains underexplored. Existing training frameworks primarily optimize for single-agent scenarios and fail to capture the graph-structured nature of MARL. This fundamental mismatch leads to three MARL-specific challenges: topology-induced rollout skew, critical path synchronization barriers, and dynamic training demand. papers.summary: A growing share of trading decisions is made by algorithmic agents, and reinforcement learning (RL) is an increasingly common way to build them.
